stem: A deployment team must select the geographic area where its Azure resources are hosted. Which Azure concept should it choose?

answer_explanation: Azure region pairs are designated geographic pairs used by some services for specific platform and recovery considerations.

stem: Which physical facilities contain the servers and networking equipment used to deliver Azure services?

stem: An organization is evaluating specialized Azure regions intended for particular compliance or government requirements. What should it review?
option_a: The applicable Azure region offering and its requirements
expected_answer: The applicable Azure region offering and its requirements

stem: Which management scope can group subscriptions so governance can be applied above them?

stem: A team needs to build a generative AI application using a hosted model endpoint. Which Azure service area should it investigate?

stem: A data pipeline must ingest a continuous stream of telemetry for near-real-time processing. Which service category is relevant?

stem: A team wants to determine which services and features are available in its chosen geography. What should it consult?

stem: A company wants to assess on-premises servers and plan their migration to Azure. Which service should it investigate?

stem: A developer wants to host a web application while Azure manages much of the web-server infrastructure. Which service is appropriate?

answer_explanation: AKS is Azure's managed Kubernetes offering; check current features and supported configurations.

stem: A team needs to run a container instance without provisioning a Kubernetes cluster. Which service is relevant?
answer_explanation: Azure Container Instances runs containers without requiring cluster management.

stem: A solution stores large amounts of unstructured binary data such as media files. Which service is suitable?
answer_explanation: Blob Storage is designed for unstructured object data such as documents, media, and backups.

answer_explanation: Azure Files provides managed file shares, with protocol support dependent on the configuration and region.

stem: An application needs a managed relational database compatible with SQL Server. Which Azure service should it evaluate?
answer_explanation: Azure SQL Database is a managed relational database service based on SQL Server technology.

stem: A globally distributed application needs a managed NoSQL data store and supported API choices. Which service should it investigate?
answer_explanation: Cosmos DB is a globally distributed NoSQL database offering; availability and APIs vary by configuration.

stem: An organization needs a virtual private network tunnel between its on-premises site and Azure. Which gateway category should it use?
answer_explanation: Azure VPN Gateway can connect on-premises networks to Azure over VPN tunnels.

stem: A customer requires private connectivity from its network into Microsoft cloud services. Which service should it evaluate?
answer_explanation: ExpressRoute provides private connectivity to Microsoft cloud services; connectivity and location availability should be verified.

stem: An application needs a DNS-based service to route users among endpoints in different geographic regions. Which solution category is relevant?
answer_explanation: Global DNS-based routing can direct clients to endpoints based on configured routing policies.

stem: A team needs network traffic rules associated with a subnet or network interface. Which feature should it configure?
answer_explanation: Network security groups contain inbound and outbound traffic rules that can be associated with subnets or network interfaces.

stem: A team wants Azure resources to communicate over an isolated, configurable network. Which service should it create?
answer_explanation: Azure Virtual Network provides a logically isolated network for Azure resources.

stem: A company wants to host DNS records for a domain using Azure-managed DNS infrastructure. Which service should it use?
answer_explanation: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and records on Azure infrastructure.

stem: A migration transfers a large dataset by shipping a device instead of relying on network bandwidth. Which solution is relevant?

stem: Data is accessed frequently and needs low-latency online access. Which type of blob access tier should be evaluated?

stem: Data is rarely read and can remain offline until needed. Which type of blob access tier should be evaluated?
answer_explanation: The archive tier is intended for rarely accessed data and requires rehydration before reading.

stem: A team wants to extract text from scanned documents and images. Which AI capability should it investigate?
answer_explanation: Optical character recognition extracts machine-readable text from images and documents.

stem: A company wants to classify text sentiment and extract phrases from customer feedback. Which AI capability is relevant?
answer_explanation: Natural language processing includes capabilities for analyzing text, such as sentiment and key phrase extraction.

stem: A user needs to read resource settings but should not make changes. What access principle should guide role assignment?
answer_explanation: Least privilege grants only the permissions needed to perform the required tasks.

stem: A company needs a cloud identity service to manage users and sign-in to applications. Which service should it use?
answer_explanation: Microsoft Entra ID provides identity and access management capabilities for users and applications.

answer_explanation: Authentication verifies identity; authorization determines what the verified identity can access.

answer_explanation: Authorization evaluates permissions for an authenticated identity.

answer_explanation: Multifactor authentication requires more than one form of verification.

answer_explanation: Conditional Access evaluates configured signals and policies to make access decisions; exact capabilities depend on licensing and configuration.

answer_explanation: Zero Trust emphasizes explicit verification, least-privilege access, and assuming breach.

stem: A design uses several independent protective controls so that one control failure does not remove every safeguard. Which approach is this?
answer_explanation: Defense in depth layers multiple security controls to reduce reliance on a single safeguard.

stem: An application must store and retrieve passwords and cryptographic keys under access controls. Which service should it consider?

stem: An application needs centrally managed cryptographic keys and certificates. Which service should it consider?

stem: An operations team needs to collect metrics and logs from Azure resources for investigation. Which service should it use?

stem: A team needs information about service issues and planned maintenance affecting its Azure resources. Which service should it consult?

stem: A company wants to stop paying for a temporary test environment after its project ends. Which cloud characteristic supports this plan?

stem: An organization replaces a large upfront server purchase with recurring charges for hosted compute. Which expense pattern is it adopting?

answer_explanation: PaaS abstracts much of the infrastructure and operating-system management so teams can deploy application code.

stem: A retailer wants compute capacity to expand and contract as seasonal demand changes. Which cloud property best matches this requirement?
answer_explanation: Elasticity is the ability to adjust provisioned capacity as demand changes.

stem: A database workload is growing and the team increases available capacity to support it. Which characteristic is being used?
answer_explanation: Scalability describes the ability to increase capacity as workload requirements grow.

stem: A design continues operating when one component fails by using redundant components. Which design property is this?
answer_explanation: Fault tolerance uses redundancy so a component failure does not necessarily stop the whole service.

stem: A business documents how to restore services and data after a major outage. Which planning discipline is this?
answer_explanation: Disaster recovery planning defines how systems and data can be restored after a disruptive event.

stem: An organization plans how essential operations will continue during a disruption. Which planning goal is this?
answer_explanation: Business continuity focuses on maintaining essential business operations during disruptions.

stem: A team measures whether a service is accessible when users need it. Which quality is it measuring?
answer_explanation: Availability concerns whether a service is accessible and usable when required.

stem: A service consistently performs correctly over a long period, including through recovery from faults. Which quality is this?
answer_explanation: Reliability describes consistent correct operation over time and recovery from faults.

stem: A provider dynamically assigns shared infrastructure resources to customers as demand changes. Which cloud concept is this?
answer_explanation: Resource pooling lets a provider serve multiple customers using shared infrastructure and dynamically assigned resources.

stem: A cloud platform reports resource usage so customers can monitor what they consume. Which cloud characteristic is this?
answer_explanation: Measured service tracks resource consumption for monitoring and usage-based billing.

stem: An authorized user provisions a cloud resource through a portal without waiting for provider staff. Which cloud characteristic is this?
answer_explanation: On-demand self-service lets customers provision resources as needed through available interfaces.

stem: A user accesses a cloud application from supported devices over a network. Which cloud characteristic does this illustrate?
answer_explanation: Cloud services are made available over networks through supported client devices and interfaces.

stem: A provider measures compute and storage use so charges can be based on consumption. Which cloud characteristic is this?
answer_explanation: Measured service monitors and reports resource use, supporting usage-based billing.

stem: A startup wants to provision capacity without purchasing and installing physical servers. Which approach best fits?
answer_explanation: Cloud services can be provisioned on demand without the customer purchasing the provider's physical hardware.

stem: A cloud provider's large customer base supports shared infrastructure operations. Which benefit may result?
answer_explanation: Provider scale can lower unit costs through shared infrastructure, though actual customer costs depend on usage and configuration.

stem: Two virtual machines have different sizes and storage configurations. Why might their charges differ?
option_a: Their selected resource types and configurations differ
expected_answer: Their selected resource types and configurations differ
answer_explanation: Azure charges vary with service type, selected configuration, region, and usage.

stem: A team deploys identical resources in different Azure regions. What should it check before estimating costs?
answer_explanation: Pricing and service availability can vary by region, so current regional information should be checked.

stem: Who determines which users can access an organization's cloud data?
answer_explanation: Customers retain responsibility for their data and for deciding who receives access.

stem: Who secures the physical host hardware used to provide Azure virtual machines?
answer_explanation: Microsoft is responsible for the physical datacenter and host infrastructure.

stem: Which service model generally transfers more infrastructure management to the provider than IaaS?
answer_explanation: SaaS shifts management of the application and underlying platform to the provider, while customers still manage data and access.

stem: A customer wants to deploy code without maintaining the operating system. Which model generally reduces that responsibility?
answer_explanation: PaaS manages the platform and operating system so customers can focus on their applications and data.

stem: Capacity is added to handle growth, but the system does not automatically remove capacity later. Which broader capability is still demonstrated?
answer_explanation: Scalability is the ability to increase capacity; elasticity specifically adjusts capacity as demand changes.

stem: A company uses Azure only, with no services from another public cloud provider. Does that alone make its design multicloud?
answer_explanation: Multicloud means using services from multiple cloud providers; using one public cloud alone is not multicloud.

stem: A company connects its on-premises private environment to Azure. Which model is directly described?
answer_explanation: Hybrid cloud connects private infrastructure with public cloud services; multicloud refers to using multiple public cloud providers.

stem: A team designs backup and recovery procedures to restore service after failures. Which cloud benefit is it supporting?
answer_explanation: Recovery planning and resilient design support a service's reliability over time.

stem: An application is deployed across separate failure locations to reduce a single location causing an outage. Which goal is being pursued?
answer_explanation: Using redundant failure locations can improve availability, depending on service design and configuration.

stem: A team uses automation to consistently provision and update resources. Which cloud benefit does this support?
answer_explanation: Automation and cloud management tools help teams manage resources consistently.

stem: A company needs a consistent method to enforce organizational configuration requirements. Which cloud benefit is relevant?
answer_explanation: Governance applies organizational rules and accountability to resource usage.

stem: An operations team tracks performance metrics over time to estimate future capacity needs. Which benefit is it improving?
answer_explanation: Monitoring historical performance helps teams estimate future capacity requirements.

stem: A team removes idle resources instead of leaving unused compute running. Which outcome can this support?
answer_explanation: Removing unnecessary resources avoids idle consumption and can support more efficient use of infrastructure.

learning_objective: Compare private and public cloud costs
stem: A company operates a dedicated private cloud and maintains its infrastructure. Which responsibility is typically greater than in a public cloud?
option_a: Managing and maintaining the dedicated infrastructure
expected_answer: Managing and maintaining the dedicated infrastructure
answer_explanation: A private cloud provides dedicated infrastructure but typically requires the organization to assume more management and maintenance.

stem: A developer creates a temporary environment and deletes it after testing. Which cloud advantage helps match spending to the task?
option_a: Resources can be provisioned and released as needed
expected_answer: Resources can be provisioned and released as needed
answer_explanation: Provisioning and releasing resources as requirements change can help align consumption with workload needs.

stem: A system adds instances as demand rises. Which property addresses changing capacity rather than service uptime?
answer_explanation: Elasticity adjusts capacity based on demand; high availability focuses on service accessibility.

stem: A workload is able to grow by adding capacity, without making a claim about uptime. Which characteristic is described?
answer_explanation: Scalability is the ability to increase capacity to meet a larger workload.

stem: A company pays recurring cloud charges instead of buying its own server hardware. Which spending model does this commonly represent?
answer_explanation: Cloud services are commonly consumed as ongoing operational expenses rather than upfront capital purchases.

stem: A business buys and owns physical infrastructure before running a workload. Which spending model does this represent?
answer_explanation: Purchasing infrastructure requires upfront capital expenditure.

stem: A customer configures permissions for its cloud-hosted application. Does moving the application to the cloud remove this customer responsibility?
answer_explanation: Moving to the cloud does not remove customer responsibilities for identities, access, and data.

stem: Which cloud service model offers a complete provider-managed application to end users?
answer_explanation: SaaS delivers a provider-managed application for customers to use.

stem: Which cloud service model offers virtualized compute while leaving the guest operating system for the customer to manage?
answer_explanation: IaaS provides virtualized infrastructure and leaves guest operating-system management to the customer.

stem: Which cloud service model provides an application development and deployment platform managed by the provider?
answer_explanation: PaaS provides a managed platform for developing and deploying applications.

stem: A solution uses redundant components so that a component failure does not immediately interrupt the whole workload. What is this design property?
answer_explanation: Fault tolerance uses redundancy to continue operation when a component fails.

stem: An organization plans how critical business activities will continue if an IT service is disrupted. What is this planning area?
answer_explanation: Business continuity plans how essential business operations continue through disruptions.

stem: An IT team documents how to restore systems after a major outage. Which plan does it need?
answer_explanation: Disaster recovery plans define procedures to restore systems and data after disruptive events.

stem: A team uses monitoring to forecast whether a workload will meet future performance needs. Which benefit is relevant?
answer_explanation: Predictability includes forecasting performance and capacity using monitoring and planning.

stem: A customer wants cloud charges to reflect actual resource usage rather than a fixed hardware purchase. Which model should it use?
answer_explanation: Consumption-based pricing charges for measured cloud resource usage.

learning_objective: Describe Azure regions and region pairs
stem: A disaster-recovery team deploys resources in one Azure region and copies important data to its paired region. What should the team assume about failover?
option_a: Every Azure service automatically fails over to the paired region
option_b: The team must configure and test recovery for services that do not fail over automatically
option_c: A region pair is the same thing as a resource group
option_d: The paired region removes the need for backups
expected_answer: The team must configure and test recovery for services that do not fail over automatically
answer_explanation: Region pairs support broader resilience, but customers still need to configure replication and recovery where a service does not fail over automatically. A paired region is not a backup by itself.

stem: A hospital wants two application instances in physically separate datacenter locations within the same supported Azure region. Which feature should it use?
answer_explanation: Availability zones are physically separate locations within a region with independent power, cooling, and networking, helping isolate a single-location failure.

stem: A company wants a policy to apply consistently to several subscriptions belonging to the same division. Where should the policy be assigned?
option_a: A management group above those subscriptions
expected_answer: A management group above those subscriptions
answer_explanation: Management groups sit above subscriptions, and policy assignments can be inherited by the subscriptions and resources below them.

learning_objective: Choose resource group and subscription scopes
stem: A temporary training environment contains a VM, virtual network, and storage account that should be managed and removed together. What is the most suitable container?
answer_explanation: A resource group organizes related resources for management and lifecycle actions. Deleting the group also deletes its resources, so the team should verify the contents first.

learning_objective: Select an Azure compute hosting option
stem: A company must install custom operating-system software and manage the guest OS for a legacy application. Which Azure compute option gives it the most control?
answer_explanation: Virtual machines provide control over the guest operating system and installed software, along with more customer management responsibility than managed hosting options.

stem: A team needs to host a web application and REST API without managing the underlying operating system. Which service is the best fit?
answer_explanation: App Service is a managed platform for web apps and REST APIs. A virtual network provides connectivity, not application hosting.

stem: A photo-processing task should run only when a new image arrives in storage and scale with the number of uploads. Which compute option is most appropriate?
answer_explanation: Functions runs event-driven code in response to triggers and can scale with demand, making it suitable for work that occurs when an event happens.

stem: A team has a small containerized API and wants managed scaling without operating a Kubernetes cluster. Which service is the better fit?
answer_explanation: Container Apps offers managed scaling for container applications without requiring the team to operate a full Kubernetes platform. AKS is appropriate when Kubernetes orchestration is needed.

learning_objective: Describe virtual networks and network security groups
stem: A web subnet should accept HTTPS traffic, while direct internet traffic to a database subnet should be blocked. Which Azure feature provides rules for this traffic filtering?
answer_explanation: NSGs use inbound and outbound rules based on addresses, ports, and protocols. They can allow HTTPS to the web tier while restricting traffic to the database tier.

stem: A branch office needs an encrypted connection to an Azure virtual network over the public internet. Which service should it use?
answer_explanation: VPN Gateway creates encrypted tunnels over the public internet for connections such as site-to-site VPNs. ExpressRoute is a private connectivity option that does not send traffic over the public internet.

stem: A media company needs highly scalable object storage for images and video files. Which Azure storage service is the most direct fit?
answer_explanation: Blob Storage is designed for large amounts of unstructured object data such as images and video. DNS and virtual networks provide different capabilities.

stem: A workload needs storage copies distributed synchronously across availability zones within its primary region. Which redundancy option matches this requirement?
answer_explanation: ZRS synchronously copies data across availability zones in the primary region. LRS keeps copies in one datacenter, while Archive is an access tier rather than a redundancy option.

stem: A customer-facing application needs a managed NoSQL database for flexible document data that it can distribute across regions. Which Azure service is the most appropriate?
answer_explanation: Azure Cosmos DB is a fully managed NoSQL database designed for flexible data models and global distribution. Azure SQL Database is a managed relational service suited to relational tables and SQL queries.

stem: A support application needs a prebuilt speech-to-text capability through an API rather than a custom model trained by its team. What should it evaluate?
answer_explanation: Azure AI services provide prebuilt capabilities such as speech, language, vision, and document processing through APIs. Azure Machine Learning is used to build and manage custom models.

stem: Thousands of devices must securely send telemetry to Azure and receive commands in return. Which service is designed for this device-to-cloud communication?
answer_explanation: IoT Hub provides secure two-way communication between IoT devices and the cloud. IoT Central offers a higher-level managed IoT application experience.

stem: A company must move tens of terabytes to Azure, but its available network bandwidth makes an online transfer impractical. Which solution is designed for this situation?
answer_explanation: Data Box uses a secure physical device to transfer very large datasets when network transfer is impractical. It is not a compute or name-resolution service.

learning_objective: Distinguish authentication, Conditional Access, and RBAC
stem: An employee signs in successfully, but access to an application should require MFA when the sign-in comes from an unfamiliar location. Which capability evaluates signals and applies that access requirement?
answer_explanation: Conditional Access evaluates signals such as identity, location, device, and application, then can allow, block, or require MFA. RBAC controls authorization to Azure resources after identity is established.

learning_objective: Apply Zero Trust and defense in depth
stem: A security design verifies each access request, grants only required permissions, encrypts data in transit and at rest, and uses multiple independent safeguards. Which principles does this most closely apply?
option_a: Zero Trust and defense in depth
expected_answer: Zero Trust and defense in depth
answer_explanation: Zero Trust verifies access explicitly and applies least privilege, while defense in depth uses multiple protective layers. Encryption in transit and at rest is one important layer alongside controls such as MFA, RBAC, and Defender for Cloud.

learning_objective: Protect secrets and assess cloud security posture
stem: An application needs to retrieve a database password securely, and its security team wants prioritized recommendations and threat alerts for its cloud resources. Which pair of services best fits?
option_a: Azure Key Vault and Microsoft Defender for Cloud
option_b: Azure DNS and Azure Data Box
option_c: Azure Advisor and Azure Pricing Calculator
option_d: Azure Policy and Microsoft Service Trust Portal
expected_answer: Azure Key Vault and Microsoft Defender for Cloud
answer_explanation: Key Vault stores and controls access to secrets, keys, and certificates. Defender for Cloud assesses security posture and helps protect workloads with recommendations and threat alerts.

stem: Before deploying a new solution, a project manager wants to estimate the cost of selected Azure services and configurations. Which tool should they use?
answer_explanation: The Pricing Calculator estimates the potential cost of planned Azure services and configurations. It does not deploy resources or create charges.

stem: A department wants a notification when monthly spending approaches its target so it can investigate before exceeding expectations. What should it configure?
option_a: A Cost Management budget with an alert threshold
option_b: A Delete lock on the subscription
expected_answer: A Cost Management budget with an alert threshold
answer_explanation: Cost Management budgets define expected spending limits and can trigger alerts at configured thresholds. A budget does not automatically prevent all charges.

stem: A data-governance team needs to discover sensitive data, classify it, and understand its lineage across systems. Which Microsoft service is designed for these capabilities?
answer_explanation: Purview provides data-governance capabilities such as discovery, classification, and lineage across data environments. Advisor provides recommendations for Azure resources.

stem: An organization wants to prevent storage accounts from being deployed outside approved Azure regions. Which control should it use?
answer_explanation: Azure Policy can audit, deny, or remediate resource configurations against organizational rules. Advisor recommends improvements but does not enforce deployment rules.

stem: A production database should remain editable by its operators, but accidental deletion must be blocked. Which action best meets this requirement?
option_a: Apply a Delete lock to the database
option_b: Apply a ReadOnly lock to the entire subscription
option_d: Move the database to another availability zone
expected_answer: Apply a Delete lock to the database
answer_explanation: A Delete lock blocks deletion while allowing authorized changes. ReadOnly blocks both updates and deletion; a tag is metadata and does not protect a resource.

stem: A compliance officer needs Microsoft's security, privacy, and compliance documentation for an audit. Where should they look?
answer_explanation: The Service Trust Portal provides resources about Microsoft's security, privacy, compliance controls, and audit practices. Some protected materials require sign-in.

stem: An administrator is using a borrowed computer and needs an authenticated browser-based environment with Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell available without local installation. Which tool fits?
answer_explanation: Cloud Shell is an authenticated browser-based shell with Azure CLI and PowerShell available. Advisor and Resource Health are service experiences, not command environments.

learning_objective: Describe Azure Arc and infrastructure as code
stem: A company wants to bring on-premises servers under Azure management and define repeatable deployments in a concise declarative language that deploys through Azure Resource Manager. Which pair is appropriate?
option_b: Azure Service Health and Log Analytics
answer_explanation: Azure Arc projects supported resources outside Azure into Azure Resource Manager for consistent management. Bicep is a declarative infrastructure-as-code language that deploys through ARM; ARM templates provide a JSON-based alternative.

learning_objective: Differentiate Advisor, Service Health, and Monitor
stem: An administrator needs recommendations to improve a deployed workload's reliability, security, performance, operations, and cost. Which service provides these recommendations?
answer_explanation: Advisor analyzes resources and provides recommendations in categories including reliability, security, performance, operational excellence, and cost. Service Health reports service events affecting the customer.

learning_objective: Use monitoring logs and application insights
stem: A web team wants to trace slow requests through application dependencies and see failures and response times. Which monitoring capability is the most targeted fit?
answer_explanation: Application Insights monitors application requests, dependencies, response times, failures, and availability. Log Analytics is used to query collected log data, while Azure Monitor provides the broader monitoring platform.

stem: A startup needs computing power this week but does not want to buy servers or build a datacenter. Which approach best meets its need?
option_a: Rent computing services over the internet from a cloud provider
option_b: Purchase enough hardware for the startup's largest possible future workload
option_c: Move all work to a private office network without hosted services
option_d: Replace its application with a spreadsheet stored on one laptop
expected_answer: Rent computing services over the internet from a cloud provider
answer_explanation: Cloud computing delivers services such as compute, storage, and networking over the internet on demand. Buying hardware is an upfront-capital approach, not cloud consumption.

stem: A team runs a virtual machine in Azure IaaS. Which security task remains the team's responsibility rather than Microsoft's?
option_b: Maintaining power and cooling in the datacenter
option_c: Patching the guest operating system on the virtual machine
option_d: Securing the physical network in the Azure datacenter
expected_answer: Patching the guest operating system on the virtual machine
answer_explanation: With IaaS, Microsoft secures the underlying datacenter and hosts, while the customer manages the guest operating system and its applications. The customer also remains responsible for its data, identities, and access.

stem: A small company wants to launch a public website quickly without owning or maintaining the underlying datacenter. Which cloud model is the most direct fit?
option_a: Private cloud dedicated to that company
option_b: Public cloud capacity provided by a third party
option_c: On-premises infrastructure with no cloud services
option_d: A hybrid cloud that must keep every workload private
expected_answer: Public cloud capacity provided by a third party
answer_explanation: A public cloud provides shared provider-operated capacity that customers can purchase and use without owning the datacenter. A private cloud is dedicated to one organization.

stem: An organization requires a cloud environment dedicated to itself and wants direct control over infrastructure configuration, accepting more operational responsibility. Which model fits best?
answer_explanation: A private cloud is dedicated to one organization and can provide greater control, usually with more cost and maintenance. Multicloud means using multiple public cloud providers.

stem: A company keeps a regulated database in its private environment but uses Azure to add capacity for seasonal web traffic. Which model is it using?
answer_explanation: Hybrid cloud connects private and public cloud environments so workloads can be placed in either. Multicloud instead refers to using more than one public cloud provider.

stem: A development team deletes test resources after each exercise and pays for the resources it used. Which cloud-pricing idea does this demonstrate?
option_a: A fixed hardware purchase regardless of use
option_c: A private cloud license that includes unlimited capacity
option_d: A resource lock that stops billing
answer_explanation: Consumption-based pricing charges for resources used, and releasing resources can prevent paying for idle capacity. A lock protects a resource from certain changes; it does not stop its charges.

stem: An online store automatically adds application instances when demand spikes and removes them when traffic drops. Which cloud characteristic is most directly shown?
answer_explanation: Elasticity adjusts capacity up or down as demand changes. Scalability is the broader ability to increase capacity; the automatic adjustment in both directions is elasticity.

stem: A service is designed so that a failure in one datacenter location does not make the entire application unavailable. Which goal is the design primarily addressing?
answer_explanation: High availability aims to keep a service accessible despite component or location failures. Reliability is the broader ability of a system to perform consistently over time.

learning_objective: Explain cloud agility and economies of scale
stem: A product team provisions a test environment in minutes and uses capacity from a provider that operates infrastructure for many customers. Which pair of cloud benefits is illustrated?
option_a: Agility from rapid provisioning and economies of scale from shared provider infrastructure
option_b: A requirement to purchase peak capacity and manage a private datacenter
option_c: Elimination of customer security responsibilities and guaranteed zero downtime
option_d: A fixed hardware purchase and resource locking
expected_answer: Agility from rapid provisioning and economies of scale from shared provider infrastructure
answer_explanation: On-demand provisioning improves agility, while a provider's shared infrastructure can benefit from economies of scale. Cloud services do not remove customer security responsibilities or guarantee zero downtime.

learning_objective: Explain predictability and cloud pricing models
stem: A company has a steady workload it expects to run for several years. It wants to compare pay-as-you-go charges with commitment-based discounts and forecast its spending. Which approach is most appropriate?
option_a: Estimate the workload with the Pricing Calculator and compare eligible reservation pricing
option_b: Use Azure Service Health to lock in a lower compute price
option_c: Choose Archive storage for every virtual machine disk
option_d: Create a resource group because resource groups guarantee a fixed bill
expected_answer: Estimate the workload with the Pricing Calculator and compare eligible reservation pricing
answer_explanation: The Pricing Calculator estimates planned service costs, and eligible reservations can reduce cost for predictable long-running usage. Neither resource groups nor Service Health set a fixed price.

learning_objective: Describe sustainability through efficient resource use
stem: A team finds nonproduction compute sitting idle overnight, right-sizes it, and schedules it to stop when it is not needed. Which sustainability practice is it applying?
option_a: Reduce unnecessary resource consumption by matching capacity to actual demand
option_b: Keep all compute at peak size so capacity is always available
option_c: Assume moving to cloud automatically makes a workload sustainable
option_d: Use a resource lock to stop an idle virtual machine from consuming resources
expected_answer: Reduce unnecessary resource consumption by matching capacity to actual demand
answer_explanation: Right-sizing and stopping unused compute can reduce idle resource waste. Cloud hosting alone does not make a workload sustainable; its architecture and operations still affect resource consumption.

stem: A team deploys two otherwise identical virtual machines in different Azure regions and sees different estimated charges. Which factor best explains this?
option_a: Azure regions may have different service pricing

option_c: Every virtual machine has the same global price
